question:
A pharmaceutical company models the profit $P(x)$ (in Rs. thousands) from selling $x$ thousand units of a medicine as $P(x) = 10x - 0.5x^2 + 4$.

(a) Find the marginal profit function.

(b) For what value of $x$ is profit maximized?

(c) Use both first and second derivative tests for justification.
explanation:
(a) Marginal profit: $P'(x) = 10 - x$

(b) Set $P'(x) = 0 \implies x = 10$

(c) First: $P'(x) < 0$ after $x=10$ and $>0$ before, so $x=10$ is a maximum.

Second: $P''(x) = -1 < 0$, confirming maximum.

Maximum profit at $x = 10$ thousand units.

options.A:
(a) $P'(x)=10+x$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=-10$ thousand units.
(c) $P''(x)=1>0$, so it gives a minimum.
options.B:
(a) $P'(x)=10-x$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=10$ thousand units.
(c) $P'(x)$ changes from positive to negative at $x=10$, and $P''(x)=-1<0$, confirming maximum.
options.C:
(a) $P'(x)=10-0.5x$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=20$ thousand units.
(c) $P''(x)=0$, so the test is inconclusive.
options.D:
(a) $P'(x)=x-10$
(b) Profit is maximized at $x=10$ thousand units.
(c) $P'(x)$ changes from negative to positive, so it gives a minimum.
